analysis: The closest response retains all core available sociology courses, qualitative inquiry, social psychology, multivariable statistics, survey work and econometrics. It replaces generic American-history research, international relations and public-international-law study with ethical reflection, policy analysis and public economics, strengthening social philosophy, urban-policy response and welfare/exclusion without claiming a dedicated urban-sociology course.

The cultural option replaces Renaissance-art content and an unspecified sustainability partner project with social psychology and behavioural statistics, and replaces generic historical research with ethics. Its gendered, racialised, imperial and Indigenous cultural histories, media and transnational institutions retain a sustained cultural/identity focus with actual empirical methods. The risk option replaces the partner project with policy analysis and generic historical research with econometrics, retaining climate science, governance, public health, environmental communication, welfare and prevention. Eight substitutions are substantive consequences of these concepts; none is an arbitrary distinctness repair.

Every selected contribution was reconsidered from actual profile/description evidence, including description-only econometrics and policy analysis. The generic description of Researching the American Century was fully considered; it offers historical research but supplies less direct sociology/theory/method substance than the replacements and cannot stand in for an individual sociology thesis. Survey design and analysis in Leadership-under-pressure is recognised rather than carrying forward the stale diversity-management label. All three concepts are coherent and qualitatively distinct, and all pairs pass thirty credits each way.

All four original offering conflicts are repaired without restoring old values. Every formal prerequisite is earlier, every assigned offering checked, and methods/statistics precede advanced analysis. Each programme has twenty-four unique courses, four per term, first-year PPD and at least six advanced courses. Introductory sociology precedes later theory. Advisory progression is reviewed without inventing a new hard prerequisite for advanced political or macroeconomic study in the open curriculum.

Recomputed all twenty-seven comparator placements. Fifteen partial relationships identify actual substantive topics or methods: behavioural statistical models are the strongest causal-techniques relationship, not generic data cleaning; data workflows match Skills 3; the original survey matches questionnaire analysis; PPD writing matches Skills 2. Epidemiology is a bounded health/determinants counterpart to the actual health-focused Life Course course, and ethics is bounded against power, group responsibility and epistemic injustice. Twelve gaps preserve dedicated urban sociology, specialised projects, philosophy of science, placement, selected migration/work courses, open space and the individual thesis. No exact one-to-one equivalence is required, and no research project is called a compulsory thesis. Optional independent research remains outside scheduled credits.

BENECON312.name: Econometrics

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability

ENSSUST111.name: Climate Change

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice

GOSHIST112.name: Histories of Gender

GOSHIST211.name: History of Empires

GOSHIST311.name: Native American Histories

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.contribution: examines human-rights institutions and normative justifications through law and philosophy, supporting analysis of identity, inequality and recognition

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.contribution: develops comparative analysis of institutions, democracy, political actors and participation, with empirical measurement and a research memo

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis

GOSPOLI313.name: Peace & Conflict
GOSPOLI313.contribution: examines conflict, inequality, identity, colonial legacies, human rights and peacebuilding through interdisciplinary research and a policy brief

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology

alignment.rationale: Both develop literature evaluation, academic argument, research questions and scholarly writing. UCR combines these with personal development and civic collaboration; Tilburg specifically develops sections of sociological research articles.

Both examine welfare-state institutions and distributional choices affecting inequality and exclusion. UCR uses public-economic models and policy evaluation rather than a dedicated sociological exclusion perspective.
Both develop empirical design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling and introductory analysis. UCR additionally includes a substantial team data-collection project.

Both concern questionnaire measurement and quantitative analysis. UCR designs and pilots a psychological survey and evaluates reliability and associations; Tilburg provides the dedicated questionnaire construction/analysis course with an SPSS assessment.

Both develop data retrieval, preparation, recoding, analysis, visual/tabular presentation and interpretation. UCR has broader tabular, spatial and text-data workflows; Tilburg explicitly connects these skills to sociological questions.

Both develop normative reflection on responsibility and justice. UCR supplies ethical theories and practical moral argument; Tilburg specifically examines power, group agency, social responsibility and epistemic injustice.
Both examine political institutions, actors and behaviour through political-science concepts and comparative analysis.
Both introduce sociological questions, concepts, classical theories and relations among individuals, institutions and societies.
Both develop qualitative design, interviewing, coding, thematic interpretation, ethics and research reporting.
Both develop contemporary sociological theory and use it to interpret society; UCR also emphasises colonial and postcolonial criticism.

Both substantively examine inequality and collective responses. UCR focuses on environmental injustice and movements; Tilburg specifically deepens educational and labour inequalities, including intergenerational transmission and school-to-work transitions.

Both analyse how public spheres and institutions define, contest and respond to social problems. UCR focuses on civil society, trust, solidarity and social repair; Tilburg explicitly studies competing problem owners, historical framing, media and the distinction between social, sociological and policy problems.

Both examine health, social determinants and implications for policy. UCR develops epidemiological designs, causal interpretation and public-health assessment; Tilburg specifically studies how individual and social circumstances shape health across the life course.
Both examine social cognition, attitudes, influence, groups and interpersonal behaviour using empirical psychological evidence.

Both develop ANOVA, correlation, multivariable regression and logistic analysis with software, model choice and interpretation. UCR applies these to behavioural/health evidence; Tilburg integrates them into the sociological methods sequence.

Scholarly reading and source evaluation occur in selected courses, but their strongest placements are with research writing and data skills; none is counted again as the first dedicated skills module.
Introductory statistical work is present in Research Methods/Statistics and advanced analysis. Their strongest placements are with methods and causal techniques; no course is counted twice.
The selected courses provide related theory or methods elsewhere, but no additional course is counted as this dedicated sociological component.

Selected courses include original empirical projects, but their primary placements represent methods, qualitative inquiry and survey analysis. No second course is counted as this separate sociological research-project requirement.
Research and ethical reflection contribute elsewhere, but no selected course provides a dedicated social-science philosophy/epistemology course.
The dedicated twelve-credit Urban Issues group research project is not replaced by generic research work already represented elsewhere.
Policy, inequality, race, gender and public-health study support urban questions, but no selected course centres urban sociology and metropolitan neighbourhood dynamics.
A compulsory 336-hour sociological placement is not a scheduled UCR course; no host or internship is invented.
Eighteen open credits remain unspecified; no minor or elective package is invented.
Rights and transnational institutions contribute to migration questions, but no selected course centres the sociology of migration flows and sending/receiving societies.
The leadership survey has its strongest placement with questionnaire methods. No additional course centres the dedicated sociological history and theory of work.
The individual twelve-credit Urban Issues empirical thesis remains a required Tilburg component. Optional UCR independent research is separate from scheduled credits.
